title: Sequence context specific DNA de-methylation shapes progression of IDH mutant oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas
projectDescription: Background: Aggressiveness guides treatment in IDH-mutant gliomas. Objective grading of oligodendrogliomas is therefore urgently needed. Material and Methods: 211 primary and recurrent resections from 111 oligodendroglioma patients were collected, complemented with 91 samples for validation. Samples were subjected to Ki-67 staining, proteomics and DNA-methylation profiling. Data were analyzed using various multivariate differential models and algorithms. Results & conclusion: We developed CGCψ, a continuous grading coefficient independent of tumor typing, and demonstrate its prognostic value in oligodendrogliomas. Its prognostic value outperformed WHO grade at tumor recurrence. CGCψ is linked to large scale DNA de-methylation, but increased DNA methylation of polycomb transcription factors, aging, Ki-67, and losses on chr4 and chr9p. DNA de-methylation at tumor recurrence/higher grade is sequence context specific and associated with TET recognition sites. Both oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas progress along this shared epi-genetic axis. Oligosarcomas are characterized by a high CGCψ and low tumor purity.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Two 10 µm FFPE tissue sections were used for proteomics analysis. Samples were deparaffinated by sequential incubation in 900 µL heptane, 900 µL 100% EtOH, 500 µL 90% EtOH and 200 µL 75% EtOH (5 min at 25°C each). Sample pellets were stored at -80°C. Following, the pellets were resuspended in 100 µL lysis buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.2 + 40 mg/ml SDS +25 mM DTT) and incubated for 60 min at 95°C, 1000 rpm. 150-200 mg of glass beads (Merck) were added to each sample and further lysis was performed using the TissueLyser II (Qiagen) 2x 2 min at 30 Hz. Samples were spun down and further incubated for 30 min at 95°C, 1000 rpm, followed by sonication using HIFU for 1 min , 100% Amplitude and 70% Cycle. Next, samples were briefly cooled down, spun down for 10 min at 16 000g and the supernatant was transferred to a fresh tube. Protein concentrations were measured using Lunatic spectrophotometer (Unchained Labs) and 10 mM chloroacetamide was added to the samples for 30 min in the dark at 30°C and 600 rpm. Peptide purification was performed using the SP3 workflow implemented on a King Fisher Flex system (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Sample plate was prepared by resuspending between 33-273 µg of protein in 150 µL of 60% EtOH. For each sample 500 µg of SpeedBead Magnetic Carboxylate Modified Particles mixture (Cytiva) were washed 3x at 5 µg/mL, resuspended in 100 µL of MilliQ and transferred to a King Fisher 96 deep-well plate. Sample and bead plate were inserted into the King Fisher along with 3 wash plates containing 150 µL 80% EtOH. Sample digestion was performed in a plate overnight at 37°C 300 rpm using 1 µg of trypsin per sample. For sample elution, the plate was placed back into King Fisher together with elution plate 2 (MilliQ) and the run was resumed. Samples from trypsin and elution plate 2 were pooled into a fresh tube, dryed in a SpeedVac and resuspended in 40 µL MS buffer (3% ACN/0.1% FA). Peptide concentrations were measured on Lunatic. Finally, 0.3 µg of peptides were loaded on Evotips (Evosep) according to manufacturer’s instructions. Peptides were separated on an EvoSep One liquid chromatography system with a 44 min gradient and 0.5 µL/min flow rate. Samples were analysed with a timsTOF Pro mass spectrometer (Bruker) using 1.1s cycle time diaPASEF scan mode. Precursor mass range was set to 100 – 1700 m/z and the ion mobility range to 0.6 – 1.6 Vs/cm2. The ramp and accumulation time were set to 100 ms. Fragment ion mass range was 400 – 1201 Da and the ion mobility range of 0.6-1.43 Vs/cm2 was used. Collision energy was 1/K0 = 0.6 at 20eV and 1/K0 = 1.6 at 59 eV. Sixteen 26 Da sized precursor isolation windows were set between 400-801 Da and 800-1201 Da each, with 1Da window overlap.
dataProcessingProtocol: Protein identification and quantification was performed using DIA-NN v1.8.2 at 1% FDR threshold. A library-free search was done against human 1 sequence per gene database (downloaded from Uniprot). The precursor and fragment ion m/z ranges were 400 – 1500 and 200 - 1800 respectively, with precursor charges ranging from 2 to 3. Mass accuracy and MS1 accuracy were set to 20 and 15 ppm respectively. Trypsin was selected for enzymatic digestion and only 1 missed cleavage was allowed. Cysteine carbamidomethylation was considered as fixed modification while oxidation of methionines was a considered variable modification. From the DIA-NN output, per-peptide intensities were transformed into 8.070 protein-wise intensities using the prolfqua R package. Control entries and entries lacking HUGO gene annotations were excluded. Proteins with more than 50% N/A values were excluded. Intensities were log2 transformed and per-sample robust scaled using median and IQR. In total, 6.540 proteins were available for downstream analysis. Limma 58 was used for statistical comparison with CGCψ as continuous factor. After CGCψ was scaled using the scale function, protein expression was considered significant with an FDR adjusted p-value < 0.01 and |log2FC|>0.5. R v4.4.2 was used for data processing, including the tidyverse, patchwork, survival, survminer, ggrepel, ggbeeswarm, factoextra, pROC, glmnet and ggpubr libraries (https://github.com/yhoogstrate/glass-od).
